chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Imran al-Daqqaq (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated to us, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid (whose title was Shahab al-Sayrafi), from Dawud ibn al-Qasim al-Ja'fari, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): May I be sacrificed for you,
What is al-Samad? He said: The Master to whom one remains firm, in the less and the more (fortunate).

key_terms.الصَّمَدُ: Al-Samad (The Master/One to whom reliance is made)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of al-Samad in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates 'al-Samad' not merely as self-sufficient, but as the ultimate object of reliance and stability for creation. This definition highlights the dynamic relationship between the Creator and the created, emphasizing that all beings, regardless of their state of need or sufficiency, return to Him as their fixed point of reference. It underscores the Shia theological understanding of divine dependence, where 'Samad' implies both absolute independence and the role of the ultimate refuge.
